Which statement is correct?

options.A: Private goods are both non-rival and non-excludable.
options.B: Private goods are only provided by the private sector.
options.C: Public goods are both non-rival and non-excludable.
options.D: Public goods do not incur opportunity costs.

questions.questionText: Below are two statements.
What is a characteristic of money but not a function of money?

options.A: medium of exchange
options.C: standard of deferred payment
options.D: store of value

questions.questionText: In the UK, attempts to encourage people to change from road to rail travel by the introduction of a system of road pricing were forecast to have little effect because ‘people like using their cars too much’. How would this forecast be explained?

options.A: The price elasticity of demand for cars is high.
options.B: The price elasticity of demand for petrol is high.
options.C: The price elasticity of demand for rail travel is low.
options.D: The price elasticity of demand for car travel is low.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve for a product with unitary price elasticity. price D O quantity What will happen with such a curve?

options.A: A fall in price will bring about an increase in total expenditure on the product.
options.B: A fall in price will bring about an increase in sales but a fall in total expenditure on the product.
options.C: As the price rises, total expenditure on the product will stay the same.
options.D: As the price rises, total expenditure on the product will rise and then fall.

questions.questionText: A government reduces income tax but at the same time raises the rate of sales tax (VAT). What are the likely effects on the demand and supply of a normal good? demand supply

options.A: decreases decreases
options.C: increases decreases
options.D: increases increases

questions.questionText: An increase in the popularity of air conditioning units has resulted in their price increasing by 20%. In response to this the quantity supplied increased by 30%. What can be concluded from this?

options.A: price elasticity of supply = 0
options.C: price elasticity of supply = 1
options.D: price elasticity of supply > 1

questions.questionText: Which change does not have an immediate effect on the position of the demand curve for a product?

options.A: a fall in the price of a complementary product
options.B: a range of new products entering the market
options.C: a rise in the labour costs of its production
options.D: an increase in the price of a substitute product

questions.questionText: When demand for a good falls, its price falls. What is the function of the price fall?

options.A: to eliminate shortages
options.C: to send a signal to producers
options.D: to stimulate a further fall in demand

questions.questionText: A firm estimates that the price elasticity of supply of its product is 0.4. Should the firm be concerned by this figure?

options.A: No, as it implies that the firm will be able to raise revenue by raising price.
options.B: No, as it suggests there are few substitutes for the product.
options.C: Yes, as it means that demand for its product is increasing at a slow rate.
options.D: Yes, as it shows that the firm is not able to adjust supply easily when demand changes.

questions.questionText: A government decides to privatise a state-owned company. What should the government do to try to ensure that this will result in an improvement in efficiency?

options.A: allocate vouchers to all citizens entitling them to a share in the ownership of the company
options.C: impose a maximum profit margin
options.D: increase business tax rates

questions.questionText: In which economic context is the term ‘protectionism’ usually applied?

options.A: the protection of consumers against excessive prices
options.B: the protection of employees against exploitation by multinational companies
options.C: the protection of local producers against foreign competitors
options.D: the protection of the foreign exchange rate against currency speculators

options.A: a fall in its direct taxes

options.C: a rise in its interest rates
options.D: a rise in its imports
